question: does `overlay=x:y` put the picture at x,y?
answer: No. On both binaries the ORIGIN is floored to the even grid while the size is kept: overlay=5:5 of an 11x11 rect lands at 4,4 still measuring 11x11. The behaviour is format-independent (measured on yuv420p, yuv444p and rgb24), so it is not a chroma-subsampling artefact of the OUTPUT format.
consequence: The emitted command and the rendered file are not the same statement of where a still goes. Q1 compares the command — 0.000px, and that IS the contract the two implementations share. Q2 compares the file, and inherits up to 1px per axis whenever the quantised origin is odd. This is EXPORT-SIDE and PRE-EXISTING: a property of `overlay` present at B0 and in every release that shipped this pipeline. Iterations 1 and 2 never saw it because their fixtures were all even-aligned (192,108 / 960,216 / 480,270) — the same fixture-regime blindness this round exists to remove, one level down in the instrument.
proposedFix: Floor the ORIGIN to even in the shared quantiser (overlayBoxQuantise.ts + overlay_box.py), exactly as the SIZE is already rounded to even by ensure_even_dimensions. The rendered pixels do not move — FFmpeg was already flooring — so it is export-output-preserving; it only makes the emitted command honest and lets the preview land on the same pixel. NOT done in this node: it needs the golden vectors regenerated, two guard vectors updated, Q1/Q2/Q3/Q6/B3 re-run AND the desktop package rebuilt (W1 pins the package to the working tree), and shipping that unverified would be worse than handing over a measured, re-runnable finding.
